runtime_boundary: Represents the self-hosted Text Embeddings Inference server. Hugging Face Inference Endpoints, which can deploy this server on Hugging Face's managed infrastructure, is a separate service boundary. Text Generation Inference is Hugging Face's sibling runtime for causal language-model generation; its repository is archived and excluded from this collection, and this record does not stand in for it, since embedding, classification, and reranking are a distinct workload from generation.
model_management: Models are pulled from Hugging Face Hub repositories by model ID and revision, or loaded from a local directory produced by Transformers' or Sentence Transformers' save_pretrained. An HF_TOKEN grants access to private or gated repositories, and a documented air-gapped path mounts pre-downloaded weights as a volume; there is no runtime-managed model store beyond the shared Hugging Face Hub cache.
hardware_requirements: Documented images target x86_64 and aarch64 CPUs, with dedicated ONNX and Intel MKL backends, NVIDIA GPUs from Turing through Blackwell (CUDA compute capability 7.5 or higher; Volta and older are unsupported), Apple Silicon through Metal, and AMD Instinct GPUs through ROCm, which the project marks experimental.
operational_controls: Startup flags bound concurrency and batching (--max-concurrent-requests, --max-batch-tokens, --max-batch-requests, --max-client-batch-size), gate access with --api-key, and configure payload limits and CORS. The server exposes Prometheus metrics on a dedicated port, OpenTelemetry distributed tracing, and /health and /info endpoints for operators.
strengths: Serves dense embeddings, SPLADE sparse embeddings, sequence classification, and cross-encoder reranking from one runtime, through dedicated /embed, /embed_sparse, /rerank, /predict, and /similarity endpoints alongside an OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings route.

Ships prebuilt Docker images tuned to specific GPU architectures (Turing, Ampere, Ada Lovelace, Hopper, Blackwell) plus CPU, ARM64, and experimental ROCm images, so operators can match a container to their exact hardware.
Production-oriented observability is built in: Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry tracing, and a gRPC API as a high-throughput alternative to HTTP.
tradeoffs: Model format support is narrower than generative-model runtimes: only Safetensors and ONNX weight loading are documented, with no quantization-format ecosystem comparable to GGUF, AWQ, or GPTQ.
There is no documented multi-GPU or distributed-serving mode; scaling beyond one accelerator means running and load-balancing multiple instances rather than a runtime-native parallelism strategy.
ROCm support is explicitly experimental, and GPUs below CUDA compute capability 7.5 are unsupported.
license_note: The repository publishes a single Apache-2.0 LICENSE file at its root covering the router, core, and backend crates; no component carries a separate license.
